raw_comment: I have noticed a consistent downward trend in revenue. In 2019, the revenue was $2.6 billion, but it has dropped to $1.6 billion this year. I am curious about the reasons behind this drastic decline. Could it be that fewer people are going to theaters or paying for movies as they once did? Is it due to a loss of interest or the rise of pirating websites? Perhaps it is related to dissatisfaction with current movie releases, as many recent films have not resonated well with the public. Is this a result of a lack of appreciation for the subject matter, or do audiences simply want to see different types of content? It’s also possible that people are watching fewer movies overall. This situation impacts my family and friends because we often discuss our favorite and least favorite films. We represent the target audience for these releases, and our preferences ultimately influence their success. "Busts at the Box Office"

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
In the graph, I notice that the revenue for the movies has gone downhill ever since 2019. Over time the graph started getting smaller, hinting that they are making less money. I also notice that in recent years they have made the least amount of money then before, In 2019 making 2.6 billion to 2025 making 1.6 billion.

What do you wonder ?
I wonder why their revenue started declining. They continued to produce movies but making a whole lot less money. Could the public not be interested in movies anymore? Do people not have time ? Or are movies not like how they used to be?

How do you think your own summer movie going habits,and those of your friends and family relate to this graph?
	I think my own summer movie going habits and those of my friends and family relate to this graph by showing that we dont really watch movies anymore. Most people spend their days watching videos on their phones or scrolling through social media. So people who make these movies arent making as much money as before.

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
In this graph, I notice how most of the summer movies coming out were of the Disney franchise. The ones in 2019 seemed to earn the most revenue, and as the years went on the revenue began to decline. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder if this is because movies became more popular to watch at home on demand or on other apps instead of going to theaters. I also wonder if the movies could have had less promo or better advertisements than others, which caused them to become popular or not. 

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
My moviegoing habits relate to this because I used to go to the movies much more often when I was younger than currently. Now, because of how busy I usually am during the summer, I wait for movies to come out on TV and watch them at home with my friends or family. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea. 
Go Out or Stay In: Summer Movies are Less Popular, So Are They're Revenues

raw_comment:
In this graph, I notice multiple movies. Below each movie is the year it was released. Above each movie is an amount of money. There is a gap and the graph excludes 2020 and 2021. This is most likely because these years were during the Covid Pandemic and the movie industry was taking a toll. No one was going to see movies in the movie theater. Besides this outlier, as the years go on, the amount of money and movies decreases. 

I wonder what factors contributed to the decline of movies produced and the amount of money made each year. Maybe it is because of the changes in each generation. Many people prefer to watch movies at home. Also maybe the new movies coming out were not as interesting or didn’t get as much attention as the movies from 2019.

I definitely go to movie theaters to watch movies less than I used to. My family and I usually wait for movies to come out on our TV. I’m sure many people can relate. This may be contributing to the decline in the profit of movies throughout the years. 

Movie Theater or Couch Potato?

What Do You Notice?: I notice that each column within the graph shows the top 5 movies of each year in terms of revenue. The years are ordered from the farthest, 2019 to now which is 2025. I also notice that coincidentally its also ordered by revenue with the most revenue gaining year being on the left and each year after gaining less. I also notice that they skipped both 2020 and 2021.

What Do You Wonder?: Some things I wonder are why did the graph skip out on the years 2020 and 2021. Could it have been because of Covid’s quarantine effects? I also wonder why throughout the years summer movies have generated less money. Could it be due to the rise of Online Streaming Services like Amazon Prime and Disney+?

How Does This Relate to You and Your Community?: This relates to my community because many people within my town watch movies in theaters and frequently talk about recently coming out movies. Despite this though, many people within my town aren’t really going to theaters much anymore and instead are dedicating their time towards watching movies on streaming services instead.

1.  The graph is skewed to the right in the way it slants, each year
getting less and less with less value in pricing. This could be in relation to the script writing strike in
hollywood production writing as well? You can see also that certain movies have the whole image shown
while others have less of the full image. this could show that the larger the movie image the more
important and more revenue that film did in comparison to the others, that the lowest are the highest
revenue and the higher up it goes the less the movie did in popularity.

different variety in the genres as well as the different sequels that have been made. However, for me I find the theatre just not a place where I enjoy the movie as

theatre. I would say this could impact the graph as the less someone goes to the theatre the less revenue
and popularity its going to get right when its released. I also think that because of busy lives that get more and more hectic in the
high school life so you have less time for movies then before. 
beach.

raw_comment:
What do I notice?

I notice that as the years go by, revenue keeps decreasing. Something that called out to me was the fact that in 2025; when all movies were action/live, no one really went to watch, compared to prior years when people went to see live action movies and animated as well. I also notice how each movie poster has a different size to them. Majority of these movies are either remakes or sequels. 

What do I wonder?

I wonder why the year 2025 did bad in revenue compared to prior years. What made people this year not want to see movies in theaters? Does this affect filming directors and their ability to make better movies in the upcoming year ? Why are the movie posters different sizes?; do they each represent revenue? 

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?

Before the year 2025, movies generally looked interesting and fun. But once 2025 hit, the list of remakes made movies seem boring (at least imo) because people already know the plot. I've also noticed that throughout the years, it seems easier to stream these movies on streaming services you can pay for monthly rather than spending that money on a single movie for 1 day. I'd rather spend 15$ for a streaming app that gives me all these movies combined to watch, rather than pay 15$ for 1 movie when it comes out.

raw_comment:
I notice that 2019 was the biggest summer for movie money, making $2.6 billion. The amounts went down a bit each year after that, with 2025 being the lowest at only $1.6 billion. Almost all of the most popular movies are sequels or superhero films from Disney and Marvel. I wonder why 2025 made so much less money than previous years. Were there just not as many good movies? Are people choosing to watch movies at home on streaming services instead of going to the theater? This graph makes sense to me because I only go to the movies once or twice a summer at most. Otherwise, I'll usually watch it on a streaming platform at home. It seems like a lot of people did that in 2025. 

Catchy Headline: Hollywood's Summer Slump

raw_comment:
Looking at the graph, I can see that, at $2.6 billion, 2019 had the highest total box office revenue, while 2025 has so far had the lowest at $1.6 billion.  With Disney films coming out virtually every year, the majority of the top films are either sequels, remakes, or parts of popular franchises like Deadpool & Wolverine, Avengers, Jurassic World, Minions, and Top Gun.  I'm curious as to why 2019 generated significantly more revenue than previous years; was it due to the success of specific movies, or did streaming services overtake recent ticket sales?  Perhaps fewer blockbusters were released in 2025, which is another reason why it is so much lower. Going to the movies always seemed like such a fun activity in my younger years, but as time progresses, prices of tickets and snacks at the movie theater have skyrocketed, making me, along with family and friends, stick to streaming services. 

A catchy headline could be " Summer at the Movies: But the Couch Wins".

raw_comment:
I notice that within the timeframe (2019 - 2025) there has been a 1 billion dollar decrease in box office sales / earnings. From the dates (2023 - 2024) the total box office sales stayed stagnant, withholding its place at 2.1 billion dollars. I’ve noticed that the larger the cover of the movie is, represents the amount of money that was brought in from it. So in other words, movies such as The Barbie Movie or Top Gun, have their movie posters in full view in comparison to, say, How to Train Your Dragon (2025), as those movies did significantly better in box office sales. 


I wonder if economic pressures such as the rising costs of ticket prices could make attending the movie a significant financial burden / restraint for some?

Additionally, I wonder if there may be too much market saturation. In other words, producing sequels with already established franchises may be leading to a decline in appeal to audiences (in context of large budget films).

I also wonder if streaming service competition may pose as the number one motive behind the decline.

raw_comment:
TITLE- Streaming Scares the Cinemas: A Decline in Summer Box Office Revenue

I notice that there is a decline in the annual summer revenue from 2019 to 2025, except the years 2020 and 2021 are not included. I suspect this is due to COVID-19. I also notice that some movies have larger bars than others. 

I wonder if the size of the bars correlates with how much money each movie made, and if the movies with larger bars are the ones that made the most money. I think this because the movies with the larger bars are some of the movies I remember being very popular, such as Barbie, Top Gun, and Inside Out 2. I wonder if this decline is due to an increase in people streaming movies at home rather than going to the movie theaters. 

My own summer moviegoing habits relate to this graph in that I saw two of the movies with the largest bars in theaters during the summer, those movies are Barbie (2023) and Inside Out 2 (2024). I also think that the number of times I go to the cinema each year has been on a continuous decline. I think that nowadays many people just wait until movies come out on streaming services because it is more convenient to watch a film at home.

4.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that summer movies revenue has significantly decreased over the past 5 years. I also notice that the movies displayed on the graph are mostly geared towards younger kids. Most are either animated or apart of the Disney franchise. The others are mostly franchises that have already had a big following and are well known, so they always do well. The most visible thing that I notice though is the drop of a full 1 billion dollars from 2019 to 2025.  
What do you wonder?
I wonder what the reason as to why movies appear to not be such a popular thing to do anymore. Have there been less movies being produced or is the intended audience getting too old for these kinds of movies? I also can consider that people have starting to do more activities outside after the pandemic, since after 2019 it continues to decrease. The popularization of streaming movies can also be a factor to the decline. 

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
Thinking about it, I realize that this summer I did not see a movie once, and I usually do. At least once a summer, either me and my friends or my family will go to a movie together. This year we did not, and I feel that it is because there wasn't any movies out that I was very interested in. 
 
A catchy headline for this graph would be "Summer Time Sadness for Movies".

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
Revenue has steadily been dropping since 2019. I would assume that this is in part due to COVID and the lockdown of 2019. People were unable to leave their houses, so they had to substitute other activities with watching movies. I would also point out that the movies during COVID times are very feel-good movies, in contrast to movies like Oppenheimer and Twisters, which are more dark concepts, in relation to the demands of the time. 


What do you wonder?
Why is there such a steep drop from the summers of 2023/2024 to the summer of 2025? Both 2023 and 2024 represent a shift back into normalcy from the chaotic times of COVID, but this summer was not much different, so why the steep drop? 


How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
I have many younger siblings, so it makes sense that many of the movies on this graph in relation to my family are directed towards a younger audience. I have also found it common for younger people to rewatch the same movie numerous times. So while Lilo and Stitch may have a smaller audience, 2-12 years old, compared to the Barbie movie, 10-50 years old, due to the sheer amount of time these younger audiences watch the movies, it gains popularity. 


Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

Coming to Theaters this summer: Nothing, the Movie Industry is No More

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that through the past years, the revenue that has been made has been slowly decreasing. In 2019 it was 2.6 billion meanwhile in 2025 it was 1.6 billion. That is a billion dollars less than 6 years ago. I notice that a lot of Marvel movies are bringing in a lot of revenue. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why the 1 billion dollars have been lost over the years. I wonder if something has been happening with our society which has made people stop going to the theater's or stop watching movies in general. 

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
When I was younger, I feel like I would go to the movies more often. Another factor that contributes to this is the fact that now I have more access to movies at home because I can rent them and buy them easier. I also feel like I haven't been as interested in new movies as I used to be.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
In this graph, it shows the top five summer movies by domestic revenue, which is the amount of money they made all together. There looks to be five major movies per summer, with the amount of revenue slightly declining over the past six years. The movies that made the most amount of money during that summer are depicted as bigger and on the bottom of the graph, contrast to the ones that made the least amount, which are smaller and on the top of the graph. In 2025, the domestic revenue of the top 5 movies significantly declined with only $1.6 billion dollars made, opposing to the previous year which made $2.1 billion. 
What do you wonder?
Less domestic revenue made reflects the fact that less people are watching the movies. I wonder why there is a gradual decline in watching movies over this six-year span. Does it have something to do with the movies themselves being worse and less appealing? Or does it have something to do with the people and that they simply just watch less movies than during previous years? 
How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
I recognize a lot more of the movies that are depicted in the beginning of the graph, and I remember seeing a lot of them in theaters. The most unrecognizable movies are those of the summer of 2025, which could be a reason the domestic revenue declined. 
Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
No more summer hits

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
It seems like most summers, the most popular movies make around the same revenue every summer,
regardless of the movie's genre. Additionally, almost every summer, there is a Marvel movie in the top 5
list, occasionally even two of them. I also notice a significant amount of the movies on this list are movies
targeted towards children.
What do you wonder?
I am curious as to why this summer's movies have performed significantly poorer than past years, losing
nearly 0.5 billion in revenue compared to the past year. I also wonder if the revenue generated by the top
5 movies depends on how much social media popularity they have, because that is how many younger
people tend to view media online in today's society.
How do your summer moviegoing habits relate to this graph?
Generally, I do not go out to see movies, but during family vacation a few summers ago I recall going to
see a movie with my cousins. I also often hear about my friends going out to see movies during the
summer, but not a significant amount and certainly not as much as back in elementary school. The more
movies are viewed, the more revenue they bring in, so I think the freedom of summer makes it common
for movies to make much more than regular.
Catchy headline: Bills from Films: How much did your favorite summer movie make?

raw_comment:
I noticed that 2019 was the strongest year, with summer movies having the highest amount of money while so far in 2025 we are seeing the weakest year in the box office. I also noticed that most of the top movies each summer are sequels, or remakes that might indicate that there are fewer spaces for original movies. Another thing that I noticed was that after the pandemic numbers began to go down, which may indicate that people started watching movies at home rather than watching them in the theater. The last thing that I noticed was that every year each summer there was a marvel movie or disney movie. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder why the 2025 summer box office was so low compared to the other years before. Maybe other streaming services are starting to become more popular, or people are just not as excited about going to the movies like they were in previous years.
How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
I would say that my summer moviegoing habits relate to the graph. I usually only go to the theater if a “big” movie is released, like one in a sequel or if they are supposed to be very good. I usually wait to watch the other movies that come out until they are available on streaming services. I would say that I stopped going to the movie theater a lot after the pandemic which also lines up with the graph.

“Avengers assembled… the audience didn't"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
In the top 5 summer movies by domestic revenue graph, I noticed that some movies take up more space than others. This leads me to think that movies that are taller in the graph probably represent movies that brought in more revenue, contributing to the total. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why we are seeing a significant decrease in the revenue movies produce each year. Is this due to the fact that it's easier to stream movies at home? Platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime release films without us having to go to theatres to watch them.

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
I think that when my friends and I were younger, we watched more movies in the theatre because that was the only way we could watch them, but now in recent years, movies are way more accessible to us - I only went to the theatre once this summer, while in past years I went multiple times. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Would You Rather Catch a Movie at the Theater or Stream It from Your Sofa?

	I notice that movie revenue has gone down since 2019. Although each year shows five movies, each varies within the year; an individual's movie popularity significantly affects the graph. If one summer had one big hit, it would make more revenue for the year.
What do you wonder?
	Why were 2020 and 2021 not featured? I would like to know if the graph shows movies from streaming services (Netflix, Hulu, Prime) and not just movies shown in theaters.
How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends, and family, relate to this graph?
	My moviegoing habits correlate with the graph. I have seen most of the big hits in theaters when they came out. Like my friends and family (to my best knowledge), I have heard/seen more about the movies with more revenue over the years.
Catchy headline:
	Big Screen, Smaller Profits: The Decline of Summer Blockbusters

raw_comment:
1. I notice that the graph is skewed to the right, showing that revenue is decreasing as the years increase. The different sizes of the movie posters (larger posters towards the bottom of each column and smaller posters towards the top) may represent the amount that each movie contributed to the total revenue of all 5 movies in a column. There is a gap in the intervals, as the years 2020 and 2021 are missing from the data. 

2. I wonder why the years 2020 and 2021 were not included in the data and if it had something to do with the Covid-19 Pandemic or with the Hollywood Writers’ Strike. I also wonder why revenue has been decreasing over the years, and wonder if it is being influenced by factors such as the increasing popularity of at-home streaming services, after-effects of the pandemic, or a lack of general interest in content being released.

3. The summer moviegoing habits of my family correlate to the data being displayed in this graph, as we have attended movies in the theater less frequently in recent years. As we consume more media through at-home streaming services, we go to the theater less, which makes sense within the context of this graph. 

4. Catchy headline: “In Recent Years, the Summer Heat Hasn’t Been Enough to Attract Viewers to the Theater”

raw_comment:
1. A majority of these major hitting movies in 2023, 2024, 2025 consists of sequels (Toy Story 4, Inside Out 2) or live action remakes (Lilo and Stitch, the Little Mermaid) coming from Disney, insinuating a lack of creativity and instead a drive towards easy money-making opportunities. I'm not familiar with Top Gun, but the four other top performing movies (Lion King, Barbie, Inside Out, Lilo and Stitch) all seem to capitalize off the aspect of nostalgia in their audiences.

2. I wonder why certain live action films perform better than others, such as comparing the Little Mermaid to Lilo and Stitch. In addition, Disney has been performing comparatively worse in revenue compared to previous years, so will the future lead to a new generation of novel studios and works?

3. I think what is more interesting is the lack of circulation of these movies among my friends and family compared to years past. Before, there was so much hype and popularity surrounding the movies of 2019, 2022, and 2023. However, I couldn't tell you a thing about the 2025 movies, other than the fact that they're live-action remakes. Maybe me and my friends are just maturing to not like movies as much, but I think the revenue as well shows a general sway away from movies.

4. Can Formulaic Adaptations Compensate for the Lack of Nuance and Creativity?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
Over the years, the total profits for top films have steadily declined, with the sharpest drop between the summers of 2024 and 2025. The numbers above each bar seem to represent the total revenue for that year’s top movies, and that some movies have more of their picture than others, which could indicate that the more of a movie's cover you see, the higher it grossed. 

What do you wonder?
I'm curious why the graph focuses only on summer theatrical releases starting in 2019. I am also curious about how much money was invested in these films compared to what they actually earned. Is there any correlation between the film's budget and revenue?

How do your own summer movie-going habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?
While some people I know still enjoy going to the theater, I rarely do. I usually prefer watching movies from the comfort of my own home, or with groups of people, but it's hard to find a time that works for everyone.

1. The amount of money being made each year is decreasing. 2019 was the highest, with $2.6 billion in revenue, and 2025 was the lowest, with $1.6 billion. This decline isn't shown with 2023 and 2024, because there was a slight increase in 2024.

4. Summer Movies: A Thing of the Past?

Kids are taking over lives!

raw_comment:
- What I notice:
From 2019, to 2025, there is a noticeable downtrend of money production, as peoples interests in Disney's movies also deteriorate. Disney's recent movies are less original, they attempt to chase the out generations nostalgia but fail to peak us with remakes of older movies, at this rate, these fails and flops will result in their end.
- What I wonder:
Why are these movies causing such a downfall in money production? Is Disney not listening to what the consumers want to have?
- Over the summer, I'm not the type to watch movies, let alone the recent Disney movies, none of the newer titles announced have ever peaked my interest. So I contribute to their loss of money because I haven't watched a single Disney movie in years.
"Is Disney in danger? There's no hero to save it now!"

raw_comment:
What we notice: 

Over the years, 2019 through 2025, the profit of summer movies has gone down by billions, decreasing every year. 

We also noticed that there has been a lack in creative covers, with colors lacking in 2025. They are becoming less eye catching. 

Prices for movie tickets have also increased, which could be push factor for many. People are already paying for streaming services, so why would they pay even more for one movie? 

We wonder if movie creators will either go out of business, or catch this issue, and improve. 

For us, movies that look colorful are the ones we are most likely to look into. From 2019-2022, we definitely attened more of these movies.

raw_comment:
What I notice: From the year 2019, the revenue has decreased to the year 2025. In the year 2025, the domestic revenue is at its lowest it has ever been.

What I wonder: Why are most of the movies on this list coming from a massive chain of brands (Marvel, Disney, etc)?

My own summer moviegoing habits: At my own house, we own a projector and a big screen, so it is similar to having an at-home movie theatre. I notice even with our accommodations, we still have not been going to the movies at all in many years. The only movies I will visit are popular ones that my friends want to see together. I believe that the reason comes from the influence of online streaming services and how easy it is to watch a movie at home for a lot cheaper. Movie theatres are going to slowly die out in the near future, and at-home comfort will take over.

Catchy headline: Are movie theatres becoming the next Blockbuster chain to slowly die out? Online streaming services are taking over the movie-watching industry.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

There are many different types of movies over the course of the summers from 2019 to 2025. The movies are heading in a downward direction, along with the revenue the movies generated over the summer. 

What do you wonder?

I wonder why 2025 made less revenue than the previous years, and why there are fewer movies that were made compared to previous years.  Another thing that I wonder is why 2025 has such random movies on the list, compared to 2019, where the movies correlate or have other parts to the previous Marvel movies? Could this impact the effect on people wanting to go in and watch movies?

How do your own summer moviegoing habits, and those of your friends and family, relate to this graph?

There are not as many platforms that will put out movies for free or on platforms that many people usually have access to. This can cause a decline in the number of people who will take the time to pay and watch the movie if they are not necessarily interested in it.  A lot of people are also very busy in the summer, and when people get time to get together, it’s most times easier or more preferred to watch a movie at one another's house and not in a movie theater compared to past years.

raw_comment:
What do we notice:

Over the years, there has been a decrease in revenues from the production of these movies. And movie corporations have focused on providing sequels and live-actions instead of new movies.

What do we wonder:

We wonder why these blockbuster movie companies are continuously putting their money into the sequels of already existing movies instead of creating new storylines. What is causing this decrease in quality and audience consumption?

Our personal summer habits relate to this graph by:

We have all watched some of the newest movies that came out in 2025 and we were dissatisfied with the overall experiences and we stuck to watching more of the movies that had already came out.

raw_comment:
Title: Reimagined and Remade: Franchises and Remade movies sell best. 

Notice: All of these movies are targeted toward a younger audience, maybe from ages 6-30. This might mean that companies are focusing more on the younger generation than trying to capture the attention of older generations.
In 2019, all of the shown movies are remakes and sequels. These sold the best in theaters, maybe suggesting that humans enjoy familiar franchises rather than new movies. To add to this, the movies lower in revenue are new movies and not remakes.

Wonder: Why do original movies sell better than remakes? 
Why wouldn't people like new experiences and stories, and rather prefer the same story repeated?
